messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall (kaya) — Elevated 5xx + backend timeouts observed for customer ORCA on dedicated-cluster eu-west-1. Alert: gateway_5xx_rate > 5% over 3m, latency p95 spiked to 2.1s. Link: https://dash.redwood/alerts/2126001234

kaya: saw it, i'm on it. joining metrics + logs now.

kaya: quick note — impact appears limited to tenant orca-prod on pool-gpu-42. Other tenants on same pool show increased queue length.

john: @kaya can you paste the stacktrace or logs? I saw evictions yesterday on that pool.

kaya: pasting tail of the gateway logs (masked):
```
ERR 2026-03-15T10:20:34Z gateway.go:482 request failed: downstream 502 Bad Gateway: read timeout
WARN 2026-03-15T10:20:36Z router.go:231 activeQueue=312 in-flight=98 availWorkers=6
```

maria: checking node gpus: host-gpu-7 shows 99% memory, 95% compute. OOM events for some FF model shards.

sam: @maria any noisy-neighbor signals? Top processes?

maria: top shows a single tenant (orca-training) with several heavy processes: `train_loop` holding large KV cache. I can throttle their background jobs.

kaya: customer impact? Support?

support-lynn: ORCA reported elevated error rates from their users. They're on a paid dedicated contract. They see many 5xx and have a few timeouts. Already opened a support ticket, asking for ETA.

john: timeline idea — immediate mitigation: reduce orca-training background priority, enable eviction for long-running jobs, and reroute new requests off pool-gpu-42 to pool-gpu-12. Longer term: scale pool or move ORCA to isolated pool.

ops-automaton: proposed policy patch applied: `pool-gpu-42` now enforces tenant CPU/GPU share quotas and aggressive KV cache eviction after 60s idle.

kaya: executing manual reroute:
```bash
# drain new requests from pool-gpu-42 for tenant ORCA
redwoodctl route update --tenant orca --from pool-gpu-42 --to pool-gpu-12 --weight 1.0 --force
```

kaya: reroute command returned OK. Monitoring.

maria: started throttling background jobs for orca-training (nice + cgroup). Memory usage dropping on host-gpu-7 from 99% -> 78% over 3m.

john: enabling temporary canary fallback for ORCA to a lower-memory quantized model (orca-base-q4) for latency-sensitive routes. This should reduce token compute.

kaya: can we ensure no data regressions? We should route non-critical traffic first.

john: set policy: 50% of traffic to fallback for 10m, auto-scale if errors stable.

ops-automaton: policy applied.

support-lynn: brief update to ORCA: "We've identified high resource usage on your dedicated pool due to a training job; we've throttled background jobs and rerouted user traffic while we stabilize. We'll update in 15 mins."

kaya: handoff — i'm heading to another meeting at 10:45. handoff to john. I'll be reachable if needed. :wave:

john: taking over. current status: 5xx rate down from 7.8% -> 1.9% over last 5m, p95 latency down to 480ms. Continuing to observe queue length.

maria: one host still showing intermittent spikes; i've scheduled a live eviction of the top offending process and will cordon host-gpu-7 if it reappears.

john: if eviction doesn't stick, escalate to pool resize and customer notification for potential scheduled maintenance window.

support-lynn: ORCA acknowledges mitigation. They requested post-incident notes and whether their training jobs breached the dedicated contract.

kaya: add follow-up action: audit tenant job schedules + recommend placing long-running training onto a separate reserved training pool. assign to platform team.

john: creating incident ticket / postmortem stub. Summary of actions and timeline will be added.

ops-automaton: incident bot note appended: `mitigation: reroute->pool-gpu-12, throttle training jobs, evict top process, fallback model q4`

john: last check — 5xx stable at 0.9% over 10m, p95 360ms. marking incident as mitigated, leaving in-monitor for 30m.

kaya: thanks all. will do follow-ups with ORCA and get the job audit scheduled. :thumbsup:"
